source_title: It's the only cafe in town, but it's changing lives and Tripadvisor loves it
source_excerpt:
Shona and Conrad Cook, pictured left, with their staff, have seen the difference the cafe has made. ( ABC News: Briana Fiore )
When Shona and Conrad Cook arrived in Wilcannia five years ago, they noticed two things pretty quickly: there was nowhere to eat in town and the local teenagers had very little to do.
So, drawing on their hospitality background, the Cooks decided to help solve those problems in one go by opening a cafe.
For years, Wilcannia in western New South Wales has languished under a reputation for being dangerous, prompting travellers to stop only briefly at the petrol station before continuing on their way.
The cafe is popular with tourists, tradies and locals alike. ( ABC News: Em Jensen / Briana Fiore )
But since the Cooks opened Cafe2836 in 2023, things have started to change for the historic community on the banks of the Darling River.
"It's brought a lot of tourism into the town," waitress and barista Brooke Tanswell said.
"When people do stop here [now] … they always come back.
"They say once you've come across the river … you know you're definitely coming back."
Stevie Harris was very shy when she first began working at the cafe. ( ABC News )
The cafe has a Tripadvisor rating of 4.8 stars out of 5 and reviews of the food and staff are glowing.
The cafe has rave reviews on Tripadvisor. ( Supplied: Tripadvisor )
Ms Cook said one of the biggest problems in the town was a lack of opportunities for teenagers.
"We saw the girls in the community … with nothing to do," Ms Cook said.
"Just bored … no confidence, no self-esteem."
Ms Tanswell said the cafe now employed several young Indigenous women.
Brooke Tanswell, right, with Stevie Harris, says it's a "privilege" to be considered a role model. ( ABC News: Briana Fiore )
"It makes you want to get out of bed every morning, that's for sure," Ms Tanswell said.
Stevie Harris, 16, said her confidence had grown dramatically since she started working at the cafe earlier this year.
It's pushed her out of her comfort zone, too.
Stevie Harris says she has learnt new skills working at the cafe. ( ABC News: Em Jensen )
"Not a lot of kids my age went to school," she said.
"I was the only one in my class for two years and that was pretty hard, but I kept pushing myself.
"So getting a job was a really big goal for me."
Ms Tanswell said seeing Ms Harris's confidence grow had been wonderful.
Shona and Conrad Cook opened the cafe after seeing there were few opportunities for the town's teenagers to find work. ( ABC News: Em Jensen )
Building up the confidence of the staff has been an important focus for the Cooks.
Ms Harris said overcoming feelings of embarrassment or the complex cultural concept of shame, had been a big step for her.
"It just brings a lot of happiness and joy to you when you serve people," Ms Harris said.
The cafe has created jobs for young Indigenous women like Sharlana Thorpe. ( ABC News )
Ms Cook said she had explained to the girls and women she employs that they had nothing to be ashamed of, and that speaking to customers was part of the hospitality job.
"Now they'll talk to anybody, they'll give them eye contact. It's just really good to see," she said.
The girls are also seen as role models for the town's younger residents.
"I always get told by the little kids when they come in here that they want to work here, so they all look up to us for sure," Ms Tanswell said.
The cafe is more than just a workplace, Ms Tanswell says, as it feels like home.
"They [the Cooks] are my second mum and dad … they treat everyone like they're their own family," she said.
Shona and Conrad Cook say "the girls" they employ are like family. ( ABC News: Em Jensen )
Ms Cook says "the girls are everything to us".
"We're here to help the community, and we've shown for years that we're working hard to help Wilcannia to help the young ones get on their feet.
"It's a full community effort to get it where it is."
There were limited dining options in Wilcannia before the Cooks opened their cafe. ( ABC News: Bill Ormonde )
